messages:
sara (CS): Quick weekly check-in for BlueHarbor — caching + batching effectiveness (7d window). TL;DR: cache hit ↑ to 72% (+6pp), avg batch size down to 3.4 (-0.6), cost per 1k tokens ~ $1.48 (−10%). Sharing details and asks below.

jordan (CS): Nice — can you paste the raw numbers? especially error rates & tail latency.

sara (CS): Sure. Core metrics (last 7d):
- requests: 1.2M
- cache hit rate: 72% (prev week 66%)
- avg batch size: 3.4 (prev 4.0)
- P95 latency (inference): 420ms (prev 390ms)
- P99 latency: 890ms (prev 840ms)
- 5xx rate: 0.14% (stable)
- cost / 1k tokens: $1.48 (prev $1.65)

ronan (ML): Hit rate lift looks like it came from enabling prefix caching on the churny routes (session-summary v2). We saw KV cache reuse increase. The slight drop in batch size is expected after the routing rule change that prioritizes latency SLOs.

eva (Eng): I instrumented a quick check — the coalescing buffer was lowered to 30ms last Friday which explains batch size dip. If we relax to 50ms for non-interactive routes we should see batch size ↑ without hurting P95 too much.

jordan (CS): Any change impacts for BlueHarbor’s billing/renewal? they mentioned unit-cost sensitivity in the QBR.

sara (CS): Cost drop helps the renewal convo. But Jordan: we need to keep an eye on tail latency — if P99 climbs customers get jitter complaints.

ronan (ML): Proposal: 1) re-enable 50ms coalescing for non-chat endpoints 2) extend prefix cache TTL from 20s -> 45s for session-summary keys where content has high reuse 3) enable low-overhead metadata hashing to group similar requests into the same batch.

eva (Eng): I can put a canary for change #1 and #2 on staging today, deploy to prod canary 2% tomorrow morning. tim-deploy-bot will emit the rollout events.

tim-deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: staging: 1850002400 -> prod-canary-2pct: 1850080000 (auto rollback 10m on >=0.5% error uplift).

jordan (CS): Good. Can we capture per-tenant cost delta in the canary? BlueHarbor is high-variance — we'd rather show them a conservative estimate before renewal.

eva (Eng): Adding a per-tenant delta metric to the rollout dashboard now. Query we’ll use: ```sql
SELECT tenant_id, SUM(tokens) as tokens, SUM(cost_est) as est_cost
FROM inference_events
WHERE ts BETWEEN :canary_start AND :canary_end
GROUP BY tenant_id;
```

sara (CS): Action items: [eva] launch canary + add per-tenant delta, [ronan] baseline test for metadata hashing, [jordan] prep renewal note with cost delta scenarios. I'll schedule a 20m sync Fri 11am to review canary numbers.

jordan (CS): OK. Also flagged a potential churn risk — customer reported a handful of 503s last week. Not a spike but needs attention for renewal narrative.

eva (Eng): I dug logs — most 503s are from request throttles during a 12:05 UTC job spike. Will add smoother burst policy for that tenant.

ronan (ML): If smoothing is added, we should simulate the impact on effective batching/latency with the replay harness before prod. I can run that.

sara (CS): Perfect. I'll update BlueHarbor CSM with the planned canary + expected cost delta (~−10% if hit rate holds). Will follow up with results after Friday sync. :thumbsup:

jordan (CS): Thanks team. If canary looks good, we'll include the savings in the renewal playbook.

eva (Eng): Noted — will post canary metrics to this thread once available.

sara (CS): Closing notes: main risks = P99 creep during coalescing change and transient 503s during job windows. Mitigations = conservative canary + burst smoothing.

jordan (CS): 👍
